newsitem.title: PERU: Peru arrests retired general who accused army.
newsitem.headline: Peru arrests retired general who accused army.

text.p: The Peruvian military has arrested a retired general who has frequently accused the army and intelligence services of human rights abuses including the use of death squads, officials said on Tuesday.
"Gen. (Rodolfo) Robles has been arrested at the request of the Supreme Military Justice Council ... for insubordination," Congress' Vice President Carlos Torres told reporters.

Robles' family, however, claimed on national radio the arrest was more like a kidnapping as eight people grabbed the retired general, bundled him into a car and sprayed an aerosol can in his face to stop him from shouting.

Robles has frequently spoken out against Peru's military since he said an army "death squad" killed 10 students and a university teacher in 1992. He went into exile in Argentina to avoid trial after this accusation but later returned to Peru when the government granted him amnesty.
Recently he said at least one member of the same "death squad" had attacked a local television station. The government admitted the attack included military personnel.
